utterance_understood: The expert confirms that 'WHEN DISCHARGING' flags whether discharge occurred in the period under review, conditioning monitoring and reporting obligation on discharge occurrence rather than describing how a limit behaves during an event. On intermittent or conditional outfalls, permittees are generally expected to monitor and report only when discharge actually happened; if there was no discharge in the quarter or reporting cycle, there is often nothing to sample or report against that limit. The user's first instinct was closer than the event-time alternative. The expert agrees nonempty comments are not self-explanatory from structured rows alone and would not lock discharge-conditioned applicability into a rule without permit narrative language. They also warn that comment phrases in the same field serve different roles—discharge occurrence, aggregation method, pass/fail coding—and must not be folded into one bucket.
